other_failure_modes.name: Target encoding leak
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes target encoding statistics on the training fold (`X_tr`) and maps them directly back to the same training fold. This includes the target of the row itself in its own feature, causing severe target leakage and overfitting. Proper target encoding requires nested out-of-fold computation for the training data.

other_failure_modes.name: Incorrect submission file path
other_failure_modes.description: The script saves the submission file to a subdirectory (`./submission/submission.csv`) instead of the standard root directory expected by the evaluation framework (`./submission.csv`), causing a critical 'submission file not found' runtime error.

other_failure_modes.name: Shallow copy of PyTorch state_dict
other_failure_modes.description: The agent attempts to implement early stopping by saving `best_state = net.state_dict().copy()`. Because this is a shallow copy, the underlying parameter tensors are updated in-place during subsequent epochs. As a result, the model always loads the weights from the final epoch rather than the best epoch.

other_failure_modes.name: TF-IDF tokenization drops single-digit categories
other_failure_modes.description: The agent label-encodes categorical variables into integers and concatenates them into strings for TF-IDF. However, the default `TfidfVectorizer` token pattern (`(?u)\b\w\w+\b`) ignores single-character tokens. Consequently, all categorical values encoded as 0-9 are silently dropped from the text features.

other_failure_modes.name: Hardcoded submission ID column name
other_failure_modes.description: The agent dynamically detects the ID column name from the test set (e.g., 'OBJECTID') but hardcodes the output column name as 'id' in the submission file, which will cause evaluation failures if the platform strictly expects the original ID column name.

summary: The agent developed a highly sophisticated pipeline featuring extensive feature engineering, multiple model types, and SLSQP-optimized ensembling, successfully avoiding all predefined failure modes. However, the solution contains critical implementation flaws, including a severe in-fold target encoding leak and an incorrect output file path that breaks the submission process.
